prose_updates.tldr: Two predeclared proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet yield a nonregular conventional interval when pre-period ridge loss chooses the reported role. The selected-Gaussian law gives an exact coverage map: every exact selector tie protects every symmetric Wald level, all bounded local gaps are protected exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared selector correlations, and otherwise the strict coverage-error sign is the gap sign times their squared-correlation difference. A constant-treatment one-factor Gaussian chart realizes exact protection and open strict miscoverage inside a stationary square common subclass of the Shi et al. model; its asymmetric point has limiting coverage \(0.8857757910650707\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval. For correction, early selection, a \((\log n)^2\) gap, late bridge fitting, post residual averaging, and bandwidth \(\lfloor\min(|\mathcal B_n|,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\) Bartlett studentization are uniformly selector-conditionally normal on the nonempty finite-row stabilized subclass. The expected conditional Kolmogorov distance can instead converge to one over the broader class, giving a sharp positive/negative class boundary for this paper's own split estimator.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and supplemental-proxy roles, whereas local post-selection theory does not supply the ordinary symmetric-Wald coverage law for a ridge-loss switch between two valid proximal ATT coordinates. Pointwise limiting variance margins also fail to justify whole-array uniform inference for this paper's split redesign.
project_justification.niche: The binary switch has enough Gaussian geometry for an exact squared-correlation coverage frontier, and proximal bridge algebra maps its correlations to primitive donor means, bridge Jacobians, and residual variation. Finite-row late-score and post-residual variance stabilization yields a nonempty class on which coordinatewise split-sample inference remains valid even when covariance stacked across roles is singular.
project_justification.fill: The paper provides the selected limit, evaluable coverage map, exact-tie protection, all-gap if-and-only-if frontier, strict sign rule, continuous constant-treatment primitive realizations, a proved stabilized-class correction, and a maximal converse on the unstabilized class. Together the two uniform results identify the finite-row variance boundary rather than presenting generic time splitting as the novelty.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi et al. (2026) provide the fixed-role causal and inferential anchor. The present reduced-form square moment class is not claimed to contain, or be contained in, their full structural class; the proved stationary independent-over-time constant-treatment one-factor intersection supports only a common-subclass comparison, not a claim about their rectangular West-German procedure. Leeb and Pötscher (2005) establish the broader local post-selection nonregularity perspective. Rakshit, Shi, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2025) study adaptive selection with some invalid proxies in a distinct point-exposure model. Berk et al. (2013) obtain protection by simultaneous inference over candidate models, whereas this paper calculates when an unadjusted ordinary symmetric interval is already exact. Lee et al. (2016) concern a conditional selective pivot; Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015) give model-specific Gaussian post-selection coverage formulas; and Azzalini and Regoli (2012) supply supporting even-functional symmetry. Lunde (2019) supplies separated-block beta-mixing transfer under stability, while leaving this target-specific late bridge-estimation and post-residual studentization assembly to be proved here; Andrews (1991) is the HAC substrate. The broad-class negative theorem targets only this paper's own gap-split estimator. It refutes no checked published guarantee: Shi et al. use fixed roles, and Lunde assumes stability rather than asserting the target-specific second-block theorem proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive uniform theorem requires separate finite-row lower bounds for each role's normalized late bridge-score sum and normalized post residual sum. These primitive inequalities are sufficient and exclude the diagonal rare-variance witness, but the paper does not prove that separate componentwise bounds are minimal; a weaker lower bound on only their combined variance may suffice with additional cancellation control. The theorem is coordinatewise and deliberately permits singular covariance across roles. Splitting sacrifices the early fraction of the pre-period bridge information, and no recovery of full-pre-period efficiency is claimed. Generic beta-mixing separation and Bartlett consistency remain supporting machinery rather than the novelty.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact conventional coverage result concerns two predeclared square bridge systems, ridge penalty one, stationary geometrically beta-mixing panels, fixed high-moment and bridge-rank radii, bounded root-\(n\) loss gaps, and positive ATT and selector-contrast variance margins. The positive correction additionally restricts the whole-array class by primitive uniform finite-row lower bounds on each role's late bridge-score and post residual block variances; it assumes neither Gaussian approximation nor HAC consistency and allows singular stacked covariance. The maximal failure theorem remains valid on the broader \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) and concerns this paper's estimator only. The explicit Gaussian intersection gives a qualified connection to Shi et al.'s fixed-role theory, not an extension to their full class or a reanalysis of their rectangular simplex-constrained West-German design. The actionable application recommendation is a predeclared two-candidate robustness analysis before retaining the reported negative GDP conclusion. The paper does not estimate the local loss drift, handle three or more roles, recover full-pre-period efficiency after splitting, or claim to invalidate any published estimator or guarantee.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each bridge is estimated from pre-treatment moments. The conventional procedure uses all \(n\) pre-period observations for both role selection and bridge fitting and uses fitted-score Bartlett standard errors with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The corrected procedure selects on the first \(\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor\) observations, discards \(\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\) observations, fits the selected bridge on \(\mathcal B_n\), averages post residuals on \(\mathcal C_n\), and uses separate fitted-score Bartlett estimates with bandwidth \(h_n=\lfloor\min(|\mathcal B_n|,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). It is uniformly selector-conditionally valid on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), but not on the broad unstabilized whole-array class.
